subject: Normal Mixture Models with different parameters

messages.author: 31dc03607958a62a
messages.subject: Normal Mixture Models with different parameters
parts:
Hi Rstan's Users,

I consider a data y[N,Q] where the columns can be linked or not to each other.
Also, I'm assuming that each of distributions of these columns are "2-Normal Mixture Models"
where proportions of mixing can vary from on column to another.
So, I wrote the model below to identify these different parameters for each columns.
Normally, there should be 6 parameters for each column.

data{
int<lower=1> Q; // number of items
int<lower=1> N; // number of subjects
vector[Q] y[N]; // observations
}

parameters{
simplex[2] mix[Q]; // mixing proportions
vector[2] mu[Q]; // locations of mixture components
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma[Q]; // scales of mixture components
}

model{
// priors
vector<lower=0,upper=1>[2] ps[Q]; // temp for log component densities
for(q in 1:Q){
sigma[q] ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
}
for(q in 1:Q){
mu[q] ~ normal(0,100);
}
// Log-vraisemblance
for(q in 1:Q){
for(n in 1:N){
for(k in 1:2){
ps[q,k] <- log(mix[q,k]) + normal_log(y[n,q],mu[q,k],sigma[q,k]);
}
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps[q]));
}
}
}

Execution

y1 = sample(c(0.3*rnorm(400),0.7*rnorm(600,5,2)))
y2 = sample(c(0.7*rnorm(400),0.3*rnorm(600,5,2)))

y = cbind(y1,y2)

N = dim(y)[1]

Q = dim(y)[2]

DataObs = list(y=y,N=N,Q=Q)

parameters = c('mix','mu','sigma')

library(rstan)

fit = stan(file='TestMixModels.stan',data=DataObs,pars=parameters,chains=1,iter=5000,thin=1)
fit

My questions :
- Is it correct my model for idea defined before what i want ?
- The parameters (mix, mu, sigma) obtained are much different from those observed even if the "R_hat" are all 1. What should I do ?

Bests regards

> On May 6, 2015, at 9:36 AM, Eric Innocents EBOULET <ericinnoce...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I consider a data y[N,Q] where the columns can be linked or not to each other.

> where proportions of mixing can vary from on column to another.
> So, I wrote the model below to identify these different parameters for each columns.
> Normally, there should be 6 parameters for each column.

> data{
> int<lower=1> Q; // number of items
> int<lower=1> N; // number of subjects
> vector[Q] y[N]; // observations
> }
>
> parameters{
> simplex[2] mix[Q]; // mixing proportions
> vector[2] mu[Q]; // locations of mixture components
> vector<lower=0>[2] sigma[Q]; // scales of mixture components
> }
>

You're better off just using

real<lower=0,upper=1> mix1[Q]

and then your

mix[q,1] == mix1[q] and
mix[q,2] == 1 - mix1[q]

and then you can use our log_mix function, too:

for (q in 1:Q)
for (n in 1:N)
increment_log_prob(log_mix(mix1[q],
normal_log(y[n,q], mu[q,1], sigma[q,1]),
normal_log(y[n,q], mu[q,2], sigma[q,2])));

> model{
> // priors
> vector<lower=0,upper=1>[2] ps[Q]; // temp for log component densities
> for(q in 1:Q){
> sigma[q] ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
> }
to_vector(sigma) ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);

> for(q in 1:Q){
> mu[q] ~ normal(0,100);
> }
to_vector(mu) ~ normal(0, 100); // this is probably too wide

> // Log-vraisemblance
> for(q in 1:Q){
> for(n in 1:N){
> for(k in 1:2){
> ps[q,k] <- log(mix[q,k]) + normal_log(y[n,q],mu[q,k],sigma[q,k]);
> }
> increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps[q]));
> }
> }
> }
>
> Execution
>
> y1 = sample(c(0.3*rnorm(400),0.7*rnorm(600,5,2)))
> y2 = sample(c(0.7*rnorm(400),0.3*rnorm(600,5,2)))

I don't think this is the right simulation. You just
want to draw according to the mixing proportions. So if you
want 1000 replicates with 40% coming from normal(0,1) and
60% from normal(5,2), then

c(rnorm(400), rnorm(600, 5, 2));

If you want 30% then it's just rnorm(300), rnorm(700).

But that's not a great simulation because there should be sample
variation in the mixing proportion.

And even if you're just doing a single sample, then you don't
want to multiply the values by .3 or .7.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Normal Mixture Models with different parameters
parts:
I think you need to update to the latest version of Stan.
We only added log_mix fairly recently.

You can also just replace it with:

log_mix(theta, lp1, lp2)

=def=

log_sum_exp(log(theta) + lp1, log1m(theta) + lp2)

It's just log_mix is shorter to write and faster.

- Bob

Le mercredi 6 mai 2015 15:36:32 UTC+2, Eric Innocents EBOULET a écrit :

Hi Rstan's Users,

I consider a data y[N,Q] where the columns can be linked or not to each other.
Also, I'm assuming that each of distributions of these columns are "2-Normal Mixture Models"
where proportions of mixing can vary from on column to another.
So, I wrote the model below to identify these different parameters for each columns.
Normally, there should be 6 parameters for each column.

data{
int<lower=1> Q; // number of items
int<lower=1> N; // number of subjects
vector[Q] y[N]; // observations
}

parameters{
simplex[2] mix[Q]; // mixing proportions
vector[2] mu[Q]; // locations of mixture components
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma[Q]; // scales of mixture components
}

model{
// priors
vector<lower=0,upper=1>[2] ps[Q]; // temp for log component densities
for(q in 1:Q){
sigma[q] ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
}
for(q in 1:Q){
mu[q] ~ normal(0,100);
}
// Log-vraisemblance
for(q in 1:Q){
for(n in 1:N){
for(k in 1:2){
ps[q,k] <- log(mix[q,k]) + normal_log(y[n,q],mu[q,k],sigma[q,k]);
}
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps[q]));
}
}
}

Execution

y1 = sample(c(0.3*rnorm(400),0.7*rnorm(600,5,2)))
y2 = sample(c(0.7*rnorm(400),0.3*rnorm(600,5,2)))

y = cbind(y1,y2)

N = dim(y)[1]

Q = dim(y)[2]

DataObs = list(y=y,N=N,Q=Q)

parameters = c('mix','mu','sigma')

library(rstan)

fit = stan(file='TestMixModels.stan',data=DataObs,pars=parameters,chains=1,iter=5000,thin=1)
fit

My questions :
- Is it correct my model for idea defined before what i want ?
- The parameters (mix, mu, sigma) obtained are much different from those observed even if the "R_hat" are all 1. What should I do ?

Bests regards

>
> mixEst = 0.32 0.02 0.41 0.88 0.77 0.71 0.40 0.80 0.98 0.63
>
> My constat is that mixEst is not always mixObs but sometimes 1-mixObs.
I see --- you get the usual label-switching problem with the mixture model.

> So, I think, May be, I fixed mu_1 > mu_2, I obtain Always mixEst=mixObs. Therefore
> how to put the condition in my model.

You can do that, but it can affect the model. For instance, in the posterior,
it won't allow mu_1 < mu_2 for any iteration, which you might get if the posterior
mean of mu_1 is less than mean of mu_2 but there's a lot of variation. This can
affect inference.

- Bob
